title: Trace token pressure through the serving boundary
description: Change traffic, answer length, and overload behavior. The flow shows how one product decision becomes token demand, concurrency, waiting, spend, and user-visible failure.

outputProfiles.label: Concise answer
outputProfiles.detail: A short, direct response with a small generation envelope.

outputProfiles.label: Balanced answer
outputProfiles.detail: Enough room for evidence, explanation, and a clear next action.

outputProfiles.label: Detailed answer
outputProfiles.detail: A long response that increases service time and output-token spend.

boundaries.label: Bounded queue + shedding
boundaries.detail: Wait briefly, retry a small fraction with jitter, then shed excess load.
boundaries.behavior: Protects the dependency and preserves a known upper bound on waiting.

boundaries.label: Fail fast
boundaries.detail: Reject work that cannot start inside the deadline; clients receive a typed overload result.
boundaries.behavior: Minimizes hidden waiting but reduces availability during bursts.

boundaries.label: Retry every timeout
boundaries.detail: Let callers retry once without a shared retry budget or overload admission check.
boundaries.behavior: Amplifies token demand when the dependency is already slow.

scenarios.label: Support copilot
scenarios.brief: Interactive answers with moderate context and a 12-second deadline.

scenarios.label: Document review
scenarios.brief: Large prompts, slower generation, and work that can tolerate a short queue.

scenarios.label: Interactive search
scenarios.brief: High request volume with a tight deadline and a useful concise fallback.
